title: Cohort snapshotting and smart query-throttling for heavy dashboard reads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Large tenants and long time-range explorations are driving high tail latency and read amplification in console dashboard queries. Current paginated read path issues: repeated full-time-window scans, hotspots on the metrics read store, and bursty cost for analytics warehouses. Goal: introduce cohort-based partial materialized snapshots plus a lightweight query-throttling & grooming layer to reduce read amplification and p95/p99 tail latency while preserving fresh results for interactive dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce cohort partial snapshots that cover common time-window + group-by patterns; snapshots should be incrementally updatable with <= 60s lag for hot cohorts
New read-path must route qualifying dashboard queries to snapshot service and fall back to normal query engine when snapshot miss occurs
Implement adaptive query-throttling that enforces a soft-per-tenant token budget and degrades gracefully to limited streaming responses rather than outright failures
Observe >= 35% reduction in DB read ops and >= 40% reduction in p95 latency for tenants in the canary group versus baseline
Rollout plan and automated rollback in place; metrics and dashboards for snapshot hit rate, token utilization, queue depth, and degraded-read events
technical_notes: Cohort key: (org_id, dashboard_id, aggregation_signature, retention_window_bin). Cohorts chosen by historical query clustering (see analysis notebook link)
Snapshot format: columnar compacted segments keyed by time_bucket + dimension_hash to speed range scans; TTL + compaction window configurable per tenant tier

Updater: dedicated snapshot-worker pool that applies deltas from analytics ingestion stream (kafka topic analytics.events) and writes snapshot segments into S3 + small metadata index in Dynamo/MetadataDB

Read router: console-backend will consult metadata index; if snapshot hit, serve via snapshot gateway with in-memory LRU page cache; if miss, pass through to query engine and mark cohort candidate for background snapshot creation

Throttling policy: token-bucket per-tenant with dynamic refill based on tenant tier + recent cost signals; when tokens low, we return partial streaming rows with 'degraded=true' and enqueue a low-priority background export
Consistency trade-off: accept eventual snapshot freshness (configurable lag) for large-range reads; provide explicit ‘fresh=true’ param to force passthrough for a small fraction of calls
Telemetry: instrument snapshot_hit, snapshot_miss, snapshot_build_time, updater_lag_seconds, token_fill_rate, degraded_responses_count, and per-tenant cost-savings estimate
Security considerations: snapshot storage uses tenant-scoped encryption keys (KMS) and access controlled via metadata service; no tenant data mixed across cohorts
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with infra, platform, and analytics teams. Agreed cohort key shape and initial list of candidate dashboards (top 50 by cost).

2026-03-04: Prototype snapshot segment layout validated against representative 30-day export; 3x faster range scan in local benchmarks. Prototype committed: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-console-snapshot/pull/412
2026-03-06: Implemented minimal metadata index and read router stub. Canary plan drafted: 5 small tenants + 2 mid-size tenants during slow hours.
2026-03-09: Throttling algorithm v1 (token-bucket + dynamic refill) implemented and unit-tested. Initial load test shows stable token fairness across tenants.

2026-03-10: Integration testing in staging: snapshot worker applies deltas from kafka; snapshot hit path returns expected shape. Observed snapshot build time ~18s for 24h bin (needs improvement for larger bins).
reviews: Design review 2026-03-05: PM Sara Nguyen requested an explicit flag to opt-out of degraded reads for enterprise customers. Action: add 'fresh=true' passthrough.
Security review 2026-03-07: Security flagged KMS usage and requested tenant-key scoping and audit logs. Security follow-up assigned to Marco Delgado.
Performance review 2026-03-09: Infra suggested moving metadata index to a provisioned small Dynamo table to reduce lookup latency; accepted and queued as dependency ENG-20440.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Snapshot build could overload ingestion pipelines if too many cohorts are created quickly. Mitigation: background snapshot queue with rate limit; prefer incremental updates over full rebuilds
Risk: Edge cases where snapshot staleness causes user confusion. Mitigation: mark degraded responses clearly and surface 'time_of_last_snapshot' in response headers/console UI
Risk: Hotspotting snapshot reads for extremely popular dashboards. Mitigation: LRU page cache at snapshot gateway and shard snapshot segments across worker nodes
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): run end-to-end on synthetic and replayed traffic; verify telemetry and rollback hooks
Phase 1 (canary): 7 tenants (5 small, 2 mid) during off-peak hours; observe 2 weeks before scaling to next phase
Phase 2 (tiered rollout): enable for low and mid tiers only, monitor cost and latency improvements for 4 weeks
Phase 3: opt-in for enterprise tenants; provide config UI and emergency disable toggle in console
next_steps: Stabilize snapshot build for larger bins: investigate parallel compaction and incremental delta application (assigned to eng-backend infra)
Add telemetry hooks for token refill and per-tenant cost estimation (assigned to observability)
Prepare canary runbook and rollback playbook; schedule canary window with SRE
